findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.java line 47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent UsernamePasswordForm.java (line 160) is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) taking one argument. There is no no-arg overload in the hierarchy, so the code does not compile and no build with this change can succeed.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys disabled for anonymous login, breaking discoverable logins
findings.body: authenticate() was changed from filling WebAuthn conditional-UI data when passkeys are realm-enabled (previous code did it for the user==null branch) to only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, which requires context.getUser() != null. First-visit login has no user, so no challenge, allow-list, or conditional-UI flag is prepared and discoverable passkey login on the initial username/password page stops working. The same inversion is in challenge(context,error,field) at line 137 (old: user==null, new: user!=null). The gate should be realm passkeys-enabled, not user!=null.

findings.title: Re-authentication can no longer skip username step for users without passkeys
findings.body: The skip-if-context-user-exists fast path is now disabled whenever the realm has passkeys enabled, because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() only checks global feature + realm policy + user!=null, not whether that user actually has a passkey credential. As a result every re-authentication (e.g. prompt=login) in a passkeys-enabled realm forces the extra username form even for users who can never use passkeys, regressing the previous hasLinkedBrokers-only skip logic.
